steps.content: It's night. You and Adela are in a neighborhood crisscrossed by poorly-lit streets, searching for 12 Dorset Street.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Your plan is to visit an apartment that's probably laid vacant for more than ten years?
You nod.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Why did you take me on this trip, instead of one of your people? I'm Mad Shears. People speak about me with dread.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: There won't be any witnesses here if you're attacked.
Gathering evidence is only one part of this investigation, and always has been. What I really want to know is what happened in your past that turned you into who you're today.
That's why I took you with me. It's a calculated risk.
Besides, Mad Shears doesn't attack people for no good reason. She only attacks those who have too many unpleasant memories, right? So I guess I'm not in mortal danger.
Adela smiles at your reply. The two of you continue to search for 12 Dorset Street in the dimness, and soon arrive at the destination.
In front of you is a dilapidated apartment building.
Here we are. Do you remember this place now?
You receive no response. You feel as if you were talking to yourself.
You come into the dark hallway. You click on your flashlight and shine it on the letters on the doors. Apt. E is at the end of the hallway.
You take out the keys found in the suitcase and insert them one by one into the lock. The lock is rusty, and so are the keys. You give each key a good wiggle before moving on to the next one.
Finally, by trial and error, you unlock the door and push it open.
Cough... Cough...

You're assaulted by a cloud of dust, so thick that you have to close your eyes for a second, so thick that the beam of your flashlight hardly penetrates it. And there's a musty smell lingering in the air.
Clack!
The bulb overhead buzzes into life. Dim light fills the room. You find your bearings and look to Adela. She is dusting her gloved hand with a handkerchief.
The electricity is still on. Who's been paying the utility bills?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Nobody. It's just a trick I used to save money, as many ordinary folks in Eastside do. I'm a bit surprised that the circuit is still working, though. We're in luck.
Adela leaves the room and returns shortly with some cleaning tools. She must have found them in the common area you just walked past.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Let me clear a space. It might take a while. Just bear with me.
Adela sets to work, with surprising efficiency. She takes out bags of trash, which end up next to the trash can downstairs. Soon, there isn't a speck of dust anywhere in the room.
It has taken her half an hour, and the room that sat neglected for years has been transformed. She has even put an antique-looking table and chairs, old as they might be, in the center of the room.
On the table is a faded tea set and a kettle of hot boiled water.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: This is the best I could manage. Wish I had brought some loose tea leaves. We'll have to make do with only water; I don't want to bother the neighbors at this hour. Hope you don't mind.
I didn't know you had to be good at housekeeping to be a hairdresser.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Not every hairdresser.
Adela smiles.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's usually just me in the shop. No employee. So I have to do everything myself.
Adela opens the window to let in the cool night air. It mitigates the musty smell in the room.
I feel like a guest invited here for tea or whatever beverage is on offer, and you're the thoughtful host.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: (Chuckles) It's nice of you to say that. But I know what you're implying.
Adela gives a smile that doesn't reach the eyes.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I just did something I'm good at, to make it a bit more comfortable for you. I have no memory of any of the objects here. This is just like any old apartment to me.
Don't worry. I'm gonna help you remember. It's an essential part of my plan, after all.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Well, how are you gonna accomplish that?
Adela regards you with interest, her eyes twinkling with amusement and anticipation.
You can see other people's worries when you're holding your shears. That's your power, right?
My instinct tells me that you must have had many memories connected to this place. You erased them, because they made you sad. I want to see them, but I'll need your help to do that.
Adela is reluctant. She looks slightly uneasy.
Didn't you say that ridding people of their worries is your calling? Well, it's my worry, not knowing what happened in this room so many years ago.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's just... I just don't think you'd see anything pleasant.
I don't mind. I'm used to seeing unpleasant things.
Adela sighs and gives in.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: All right then, if that's what you want.
Adela holds out her hand. A pair of shears, black with long blades, materialize in a pool of dim blue light.
You grab the handle of the blades, and in the process, feel Adela's skin. It's cold to the touch.
In the blink of an eye, the room changes.
Hair is everywhere, twisting and bending as if it has a life of its own. It's in every corner, it's floating, it's all you can see.
You don't scare easily. You've seen many horrific things in your life. Still, the sight before you sends your heart palpitating.
This is what you see?
Adela responds with a mirthless smile.
You take a moment to collect yourself. And then you summon up the courage to reach out your hand.
You see a girl. She's sleeping. Someone is pounding at the door. She wakes up with a start.
She gets out of bed and switches on the light. It's three in the morning, according to the clock on the wall. When she opens the door, a woman collapses into her arms.
The girl glances at the hook that's used as a key holder. No keys are there.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Did you lose the keys again?
The girl half drags, half carries the woman to the bathroom, where, upon entering, the woman sinks down by the toilet and vomits into the bowl.
The vile stench of vomit is overwhelming. It stinks out the apartment that the girl took great care to spruce up during the day.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Mom, you must stop drinking. Or you'll ruin your body.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What did you say?
The woman says in a cold, shrill voice.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Don't you dare lecture me. You'd better keep your mouth shut.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I'm your mother. You literally owe me your life.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: If it weren't for you, I'd still be with the ballet company, and I wouldn't have to degrade myself just to keep food on the table.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: If I don't do this job, you'll starve, you ungrateful brat. So don't you dare lecture me!
The girl has tuned her shrieking mother out by this point. She's thinking about her next-door neighbor.
This irritable overweight neighbor is bound to come knocking on their door tomorrow, demanding an explanation for the racket coming from their apartment at three in the morning.
For some reason, the girl is amused by the thought.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What's so funny? You don't approve of what I do, is that it?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Answer me. Tell me what you're unhappy about.
The woman keeps up her ranting and raving. The girl doesn't talk back. She looks up and gives her mother a gentle smile.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Sorry, Mom. It's my fault. You must be tired. Let me get you to bed...
It's a heart-wrenching memory, which inspires in you a sense of vicarious pain.
Adela looks at you, as if curious as to how you're reacting to what you've seen. You meet her gaze.
Can you recall anything about the girl?
Adela shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I have accessed a great number of unhappy memories. Nothing special about this one. It could belong to anyone in Eastside, or even in DisCity.
It's all right. You have quite a collection of unhappy memories here. Let's check out some more.
Maybe some of them will help you remember.
The sun is about to set. The woman is still sleeping.
The girl is making oatmeal at the stove. She adds sugar to the oatmeal and brings the dish to the table. The aroma is delightful.
A while later, her mother shuffles out of the bedroom and slumps into a chair at the table.
After two servings of oatmeal, some color returns to her mother's face.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Hmm...

The girl clears the table, brings out her mother's mirror and cosmetics, and put them on the table. They can't afford a dressing table, so the dinner table doubles as one. Her mother starts putting on make-up, getting ready for work.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: It's in moments like this that I feel it wasn't such a big mistake to have kept you.
The girl doesn't say anything in response. She goes over to the sink, turns on the faucet, and starts doing the dishes.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Anyway...
The woman seems to be in a good mood. She's not in the habit of initiating conversations.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Have you given thought to your future career?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Not really.
The girl doesn't want to discuss what kind of career she wants with her mother. She doesn't see the point.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What do you mean not really? You can't sit around on your ass indefinitely. You have to contribute.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: You have my looks. You can be a movie star or a model. Don't waste the good looks.
Taking to her daughter doesn't seem to distract the woman from the task at hand.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Hairdresser.
The girl gives a random answer, partly out of a desire to shut her mother up about the subject.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What did you say?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Hairdresser, I want to become a hairdresser.
The girl repeats her answer, with more determination in her voice.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Hairdresser? Why? Hairdressing is not a lucrative job.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I want to live a happy life. And you don't need to earn a lot of money to live a happy life. I'll be able to make my customers happy as a hairdresser, and if they're happy, I'll be happy too.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Instead of daydreaming about how to make strangers happy, why don't you spend some time thinking about how to make your mother happy? And your mother is unhappy, because she has no money.
The girl has nothing more to say to her mother. She knew the conversation wouldn't end well.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: You're useless.
Having done her makeup, she rises to her feet and leaves for work.

The girl listens as her mother's footsteps recede and eventually disappear. She smooths down her hair, which hasn't been trimmed for some time and has grown somewhat unruly, picks up a curl of hair between her index and middle fingers of one hand, and mimes clipping it with the other.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Snip, snip, snip...

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Worries, colorless memories... Make them all disappear.
Adela's expression doesn't change, but you can feel her hand trembling slightly through the shears.
You know she's not as composed as she makes herself appear to be. You press on, accessing another of her memories.
The girl's mother looks different. Radiant even. She has even taken out the brand shoulder bag which she saves for special occasions.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Are you not going to work?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I took the day off.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I have a date, with William.
The girl has heard her mother talk about the man more and more often over the past two months. And whenever she talks about him, she goes all smitten.
The girl has met William a couple of times. He's not as likable as her mother is making him out to be.
He's a patron of the place where her mother works. They've grown closer over time. Now they spend time together even on her days off.
The girl looks away from her mother's happy face, not interested in hearing about her mother's love life, and busies herself tidying up the room.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: You don't want to know where we're gonna meet?
The girl ignores the question. Her mother volunteers the answer.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: We're going to the Belphegor.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Oh...
It is an unusual rendezvous for her mother.
Not discouraged by her daughter's lack of enthusiasm, the woman continues to talk about her beloved.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: I still feel like I'm in a dream.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: William proposed to me yesterday. It still feels so surreal.
The girl's heart lurches at the news. A question comes out unbidden.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Did you turn him down?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What?! Why would I want to do that?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: If I had turned him down, where would I find another man as handsome, considerate, and rich?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: And he doesn't think of you as a liability. He's even promised to send you to one of those fancy boarding schools after we get married. You should be happy to have him as a stepfather.
The girl looks up, her neck stiff, her face expressionless.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I'm not going to any boarding school, fancy or not.
Her mother pauses for a second. And when she speaks again, her voice is piercing as usual.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Where else would you go?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: You go live your happy life. I can take care of myself.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: You're talking nonsense. You're my daughter. It's my responsibility to take care of you. I can't just...
The woman trails off, her eyes on her daughter's face.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: You're the one being taken care of.
Smack!
The girl's cheek is burning with pain.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: You want me to choose between you and him? You don't like him, so you're pushing him out of my life. Is that it?

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Haven't I sacrificed enough for you? Do you want to ruin the rest of my life too, you ungrateful brat?
Her mother's shrill voice gives the girl a headache. Still, the girl responds with a soft voice, like she's talking to a baby.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: You don't have to make a choice, Mom. Go to him.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: What?
Looking at her understanding daughter, the woman is lost for words for a moment.
Anger fills her chest. The words that next come out of her mouth cut like a knife.

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: Get out! Get out of my house! I don't want to see your face ever again!
Without a moment of hesitation, the girl gets up and leaves the apartment.
When she steps out onto the street, the last of the light has faded, and a cold fog is rolling in to engulf the world around her.
She wanders around aimlessly. Seen through the fog, everything seems distorted—the trees, the buildings, the pedestrians. Her hair is growing fast, trailing behind her like a black ribbon.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Cut it off, and everything will be all right again...
She holds out her hand and feels something coolly metallic in her palm.
Snip, snip, snip...
You let go of the blades. The room returns to normal.
Adela's chest is heaving. It's obvious that seeing into her past must have been taxing on her.
She keeps her eyes closed, as if relishing those memories of pain and regret.
Those are your memories. That's how you got your power.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I erased them. Now they've come back to me.
She opens her eyes, which are now devoid of gentleness and composure. She gives you a weak smile.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Thank you for helping me recover these memories that I erased.
You erased your memories and your mother's, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: Yes.
Why did you do that?

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I had no choice.
Her voice is uncharacteristically impatient.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: You would've done the same thing if you were me.
But...

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: My mother and I, we both got what we wanted.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: She wanted happiness, and I wanted her to have it without having to feel guilty about leaving me behind. So I erased our shared memories of us arguing, of us hating and hurting each other.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: And I got my peace.
You lost each other.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I didn't care. My mother wouldn't have cared either.
Adela looks at you.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: I made the right choice.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: And you don't have to feel sorry for us.
Her voice is cold and distant.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: It's about time we ended this farce of an investigation.
Adela turns around and makes for the door.
You grab her by her wrist.
Adela turns to face you. She doesn't look angry, but when she speaks, it's in a cold voice.

steps.speaker: Adela
steps.content: What else do you want from me, Chief?
How you want to proceed from this is entirely your business. It's just that I haven't got the whole picture yet. I have something to show you, and I want to hear your thoughts afterward.
You produce a tape. It's a recording of an interview with a man who has an intimate knowledge of the tenants of Apt E.
Does Adela really not care about her mother?
